name: pynet-mcp-bridge
description: Connects AI models with Autodesk desktop tools (Navisworks, Revit, Civil 3D) via the PyNet ecosystem for BIM/engineering automation.
long_description: PyNet Platform Bridge is the execution layer that lets AI models control Autodesk tools in real time. It turns natural language into Python scripts that are validated by a built-in static analyzer and executed inside Navisworks, Revit and Civil 3D through a local IPC pipe to the PyNet plugin. Capabilities include live BIM model queries, dynamic ribbon/UI creation, and controlled script execution.

tools.name: list_active_instances
tools.description: Scans the system for running Autodesk processes with an active PyNet IPC pipe.

tools.name: check_plugin_status
tools.description: Handshake ping to verify the plugin listener is responsive.

tools.name: get_pynet_ui_layout
tools.description: Fetches the full UI structure (ButtonsModules and ScriptButtons).

tools.name: get_buttons_data
tools.description: Lists all script buttons for a specific module ID.

tools.name: get_output_window_status
tools.description: Checks if the output window is currently available/visible.

tools.name: send_command
tools.description: Direct script execution in the PyNet engine (Target PID, Script Name, Content).

tools.name: send_command_by_path
tools.description: Executes a script file directly by path in the PyNet engine.

tools.name: configure_output_window
tools.description: Toggles the visibility of the PyNet log/output window.

tools.name: create_pynet_module
tools.description: Creates a new custom Tab (ButtonsModule) in the Ribbon.

tools.name: delete_pynet_module
tools.description: Permanently deletes a module and all its contents.

tools.name: deploy_script_button
tools.description: Installs a new ScriptButton into a specific module.

tools.name: update_script_button
tools.description: Updates metadata for an existing ScriptButton or moves it to another module.

tools.name: delete_script_button
tools.description: Permanently removes a ScriptButton from a module by Id.
